5"""Triton implementation of aten::_pad_packed_sequence. 

6 

7Facts verified on this target (flagtree/xpu, triton 3.6): 

8 * ``data`` is the packed tensor ``(sum(batch_sizes), *F)``: batch slot ``b`` of 

9 timestep ``t`` is one contiguous row of ``F`` elements, and with 

10 ``batch_first=False`` the padded row of timestep ``t`` is one contiguous run 

11 of ``B*F`` elements whose valid prefix is exactly 

12 ``data[off[t] : off[t]+bs[t]]``. One masked tile store per program writes 

13 the copied and the padded part of an output row in a single pass. 

14 * ``lengths`` is CPU int64 in aten, so it is produced by a device kernel and 

15 copied once. 

16Backend constraints respected here: masked ``tl.load`` ignores ``other`` (masked 

17lanes read 0), so padding is applied with ``tl.where`` after a clamped-index 

18load; ``tt.reduce``/``tt.scan`` cannot be legalized inside ``if`` regions, so 

19kernels are branch-free; a launch plus its Python dispatch costs several 

20microseconds, so small flat-layout workloads go through a single launch and 

21large ones use a full-row tile in the copy kernel. 

22""" 

23 

24import torch 

25import triton 

26import triton.language as tl 

27 

28 

29# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- 

30# metadata, one single program per call: 

31# off[t] = sum_{u<t} bs[u] (exclusive prefix sum, cumsum) 

32# lengths[b] = #{t : bs[t] > b} (batch_sizes is non-increasing, so this is 

33# exactly max{t : b < bs[t]} + 1, i.e. aten's last-write-wins) 

34# lengths uses binary lifting, so there is no per-slot reduce. LOG must satisfy 

35# 2**LOG - 1 >= T so the lifted position can reach T. Buffers are padded to the 

36# constexpr tile sizes so the metadata stores need no mask. 

37# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- 

38@triton.jit 

39def _meta_kernel( 

40 bs_ptr, 

41 off_ptr, 

42 len_ptr, 

43 T, 

44 B, 

45 BLOCK_B: tl.constexpr, 

46 BLS: tl.constexpr, 

47 LOG: tl.constexpr, 

48): 

49 run = 0 

50 for s0 in range(0, T, BLS): 

51 idx = s0 + tl.arange(0, BLS) 

52 bsv = tl.load(bs_ptr + idx, mask=idx < T, other=0).to(tl.int32) 

53 cum = tl.cumsum(bsv, 0) - bsv 

54 tl.store(off_ptr + idx, cum + run) 

55 run += tl.sum(bsv) 

56 

57 for b0 in range(0, B, BLOCK_B): 

58 bvec = b0 + tl.arange(0, BLOCK_B) 

59 pos = tl.zeros((BLOCK_B,), tl.int32) 

60 for k in tl.static_range(LOG): 

61 npos = pos + (1 << (LOG - 1 - k)) 

62 bsv = tl.load(bs_ptr + tl.minimum(npos - 1, T - 1)).to(tl.int32) 

63 pos = tl.where((npos <= T) & (bsv > bvec), npos, pos) 

64 tl.store(len_ptr + bvec, pos.to(tl.int64)) 

65 

66 

67# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- 

68# small flat-layout workloads: one program writes lengths and the whole padded 

69# tensor, so the call needs a single launch and no offsets buffer. off[t] is 

70# carried as a scalar running sum instead of being read back from memory. 

71# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- 

72@triton.jit 

73def _small_kernel( 

74 bs_ptr, 

75 len_ptr, 

76 data_ptr, 

77 out_ptr, 

78 pad_val, 

79 T, 

80 B, 

81 F, 

82 R, 

83 Tout, 

84 nume, 

85 BLOCK_B: tl.constexpr, 

86 BLS: tl.constexpr, 

87 LOG: tl.constexpr, 

88 BLOCK_R: tl.constexpr, 

89): 

90 for b0 in range(0, B, BLOCK_B): 

91 bvec = b0 + tl.arange(0, BLOCK_B) 

92 pos = tl.zeros((BLOCK_B,), tl.int32) 

93 for k in tl.static_range(LOG): 

94 npos = pos + (1 << (LOG - 1 - k)) 

95 bsv = tl.load(bs_ptr + tl.minimum(npos - 1, T - 1)).to(tl.int32) 

96 pos = tl.where((npos <= T) & (bsv > bvec), npos, pos) 

97 tl.store(len_ptr + bvec, pos.to(tl.int64)) 

98 

99 pad = pad_val.to(out_ptr.dtype.element_ty) 

100 base = tl.arange(0, BLOCK_R) 

101 off = 0 

102 for t in range(0, Tout): 

103 bt = tl.load(bs_ptr + tl.minimum(t, T - 1)).to(tl.int32) 

104 nvalid = tl.where(t < T, bt * F, 0) 

105 start = off * F 

106 start = tl.where( 

107 0 < nvalid, start, tl.minimum(start, tl.maximum(nume - BLOCK_R, 0)) 

108 ) 

109 vals = tl.load(data_ptr + start + base) 

110 vals = tl.where(base < nvalid, vals, pad) 

111 tl.store(out_ptr + t * R + base, vals, mask=base < R) 

112 off += bt 

113 

114 

115# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- 

116# copy / fill: one tile of one output timestep row per program 

117# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- 

118@triton.jit 

119def _copy_kernel( 

120 data_ptr, 

121 bs_ptr, 

122 off_ptr, 

123 out_ptr, 

124 pad_val, 

125 T, 

126 F, 

127 R, 

128 NRB, 

129 out_stride_t, 

130 out_stride_b, 

131 nume, 

132 BLOCK: tl.constexpr, 

133 BFIRST: tl.constexpr, 

134): 

135 pid = tl.program_id(0) 

136 t = pid // NRB 

137 rb = pid % NRB 

138 base = rb * BLOCK + tl.arange(0, BLOCK) 

139 

140 ts = tl.minimum(t, T - 1) 

141 bs_t = tl.load(bs_ptr + ts).to(tl.int32) 

142 off_t = tl.load(off_ptr + ts).to(tl.int32) 

143 nvalid = tl.where(t < T, bs_t * F, 0) 

144 pad = pad_val.to(out_ptr.dtype.element_ty) 

145 safe = tl.maximum(nvalid - 1, 0) 

146 

147 if BFIRST: 

148 b = base // F 

149 d = base - b * F 

150 ok = b < bs_t 

151 idx_b = tl.minimum(b, safe // F) 

152 vals = tl.load(data_ptr + ((off_t + idx_b) * F + d)) 

153 vals = tl.where(ok & (t < T), vals, pad) 

154 dst = t * out_stride_t + b * out_stride_b + d 

155 else: 

156 # Affine tile base: scalar start + arange keeps the whole tile a single 

157 # contiguous (vectorizable) transfer. A tile that lies entirely past 

158 # the valid prefix is only ever discarded by the select below, so its 

159 # base is clamped at tile granularity to stay inside data. 

160 start = off_t * F + rb * BLOCK 

161 start = tl.where( 

162 rb * BLOCK < nvalid, start, tl.minimum(start, tl.maximum(nume - BLOCK, 0)) 

163 ) 

164 vals = tl.load(data_ptr + start + tl.arange(0, BLOCK)) 

165 vals = tl.where(base < nvalid, vals, pad) 

166 dst = t * out_stride_t + base 

167 

168 tl.store(out_ptr + dst, vals, mask=base < R) 

169 

170 

171def _next_pow2(n): 

172 return 1 << (n - 1).bit_length() if n > 1 else 1 

173 

174 

175def _pad_packed_sequence(data, batch_sizes, batch_first, padding_value, total_length): 

176 feat_shape = data.shape[1:] 

177 nume = int(data.numel()) 

178 feat = nume // int(data.shape[0]) if nume else 1 

179 

180 steps = int(batch_sizes.numel()) 

181 total = int(total_length) 

182 if total > 0: 

183 if total < steps: 

184 # aten rejects a total_length shorter than the packed sequence. 

185 raise RuntimeError( 

186 "Expected total_length to be at least the length of the " 

187 "longest sequence in input" 

188 ) 

189 else: 

190 total = steps 

191 max_batch = int(batch_sizes[0].item()) if steps > 0 else 0 

192 

193 if batch_first: 

194 out = torch.empty( 

195 (max_batch, total) + feat_shape, dtype=data.dtype, device=data.device 

196 ) 

197 else: 

198 out = torch.empty( 

199 (total, max_batch) + feat_shape, dtype=data.dtype, device=data.device 

200 ) 

201 

202 if steps == 0 or max_batch == 0 or total == 0: 

203 return out, torch.empty((max_batch,), dtype=torch.int64, device="cpu") 

204 

205 dev = data.device 

206 # batch_sizes is host-resident by the packed-sequence contract; the upload is 

207 # stream-ordered before the first kernel, so no host-side wait is needed. 

208 bs_dev = batch_sizes.to(device=dev, non_blocking=True) 

209 

210 row = max_batch * feat 

211 nelem = total * row 

212 

213 bls = _next_pow2(steps) 

214 if bls > 4096: 

215 bls = 4096 

216 if bls < 16: 

217 bls = 16 

218 blk_b = _next_pow2(max_batch) 

219 if blk_b > 2048: 

220 blk_b = 2048 

221 if blk_b < 16: 

222 blk_b = 16 

223 log_t = 1 

224 while (1 << log_t) - 1 < steps: 

225 log_t += 1 

226 b_pad = ((max_batch + blk_b - 1) // blk_b) * blk_b 

227 len_dev = torch.empty((b_pad,), dtype=torch.int64, device=dev) 

228 

229 # Small flat-layout workloads: a single launch produces metadata + output. 

230 if (not batch_first) and row <= 4096 and nelem <= 131072: 

231 _small_kernel[(1,)]( 

232 bs_dev, 

233 len_dev, 

234 data, 

235 out, 

236 padding_value, 

237 steps, 

238 max_batch, 

239 feat, 

240 row, 

241 total, 

242 nume, 

243 BLOCK_B=blk_b, 

244 BLS=bls, 

245 LOG=log_t, 

246 BLOCK_R=_next_pow2(row), 

247 ) 

248 return out, len_dev[:max_batch].cpu() 

249 

250 off_dev = torch.empty( 

251 (((steps + bls - 1) // bls) * bls,), dtype=torch.int32, device=dev 

252 ) 

253 _meta_kernel[(1,)]( 

254 bs_dev, 

255 off_dev, 

256 len_dev, 

257 steps, 

258 max_batch, 

259 BLOCK_B=blk_b, 

260 BLS=bls, 

261 LOG=log_t, 

262 ) 

263 

264 # One tile per output row when the row fits, so each program hands every 

265 # core of the cluster a wide contiguous run: measured copy bandwidth rises 

266 # with elements per program (~18 GB/s at 2048, ~78 GB/s at 8192). 

267 block = _next_pow2(row) 

268 if block > 16384: 

269 block = 16384 

270 if block < 256: 

271 block = 256 

272 nrb = (row + block - 1) // block 

273 stride_t = int(out.stride(1)) if batch_first else int(out.stride(0)) 

274 stride_b = int(out.stride(0)) if batch_first else int(out.stride(1)) 

275 _copy_kernel[(total * nrb,)]( 

276 data, 

277 bs_dev, 

278 off_dev, 

279 out, 

280 padding_value, 

281 steps, 

282 feat, 

283 row, 

284 nrb, 

285 stride_t, 

286 stride_b, 

287 nume, 

288 BLOCK=block, 

289 BFIRST=bool(batch_first), 

290 ) 

291 

292 return out, len_dev[:max_batch].cpu()
